🎯 Investment goal: $542.01 / $1,000 — $457.99 to go (54.2% there). Target date (2026-07-31) is now a week past with no reset — this line will keep reading "stale" until a new target date gets set.

No positions to review today. Same story as yesterday, one day worse: three unfilled buy orders, still no stop legs, now three days old.

⚠️ Decisions needed — 3 pending orders, now 3 days stale

AXTI (2 sh @ $58 limit), SPXC (0.5 sh @ $200 limit) and GOOG (0.3 sh @ $365 limit) were placed Tue Aug 4 and are still sitting unfilled — this is the second daily flag on the same three orders, none have a stop-limit leg attached. The setups have also moved: AXTI last traded ~$67.90 (Aug 6), 17% above the $58 buy limit — the entry thesis from Aug 4 may no longer hold at today's price, re-check it rather than let a stale limit fill into a chased top. GOOG last closed ~$360.13 (Aug 5), within 1.4% of the $365 limit — this one could fill any session; if it does, place a stop-limit the same day, don't leave it naked like the CAPR position did. SPXC's current price couldn't be verified this run (see footer) — check it manually before deciding. Pick one: (1) cancel the ones whose setup has drifted and keep only what still makes sense, (2) add stop-limit legs now so a fill doesn't leave you exposed, or (3) let them run one more session and revisit tomorrow — but that's the same call made two days running.

🌍 Macro Context — Aug 7, 2026

Buffett Indicator:~230–241% 🔴 ALL-TIME EXTREME
S&P Forward P/E:19.6x (vs. 5yr avg 19.9x / 10yr avg 19.0x)
Trend:↑ Rising — sources put the reading anywhere from 220% to 241% depending on methodology, all of them in danger-zone-or-worse territory.

The two macro reads disagree in an interesting way: the Buffett Indicator is screaming historic extreme (2.3x GDP) while forward P/E sits almost exactly on its own 10-year average. That means the stretch is concentrated in mega-cap concentration and market-cap mechanics, not in a classic earnings-multiple bubble — a genuine 2000-style repricing risk still needs an earnings shock, not just a valuation one.

For your strategy: 100% cash is already the most defensive posture available. No pressure to force an entry into this backdrop just because cash is idle — the macro risk argues for patience on the pending orders above, not urgency.

Last historical episodes at this level: 2000 dot-com peak, 2021 COVID bubble peak — see buffett-indicator-history.html.

Say analyze NVDA closer to the date. No other mega-cap on the radar list has an event inside 21 days — AAPL isn't until Oct 29, AVGO not until Sep.

⏳ Pending Watchlist

No live watchlist candidates. All 5 entries in portfolio.json's watchlist[] (IQV, CELC, CAPR, VRDN, VERA) are marked ARCHIVE — closed positions kept for the record, not open opportunities. The real open items are the 3 unfilled buy orders in the "Decisions needed" banner above, which live in pending_orders[], not the watchlist. stock-finder runs Tue/Sun on its own schedule if you want a fresh discovery pass sooner than that.

💵 Cash deployment — $542.01 on the books, $216.51 actually free

cash_available shows $542.01, but $325.50 of that is already earmarked: the AXTI, SPXC, and GOOG GTC orders would consume it the moment any of them fill. Treat the real deployable number as ~$216.51, not $540.

No new entry suggestion today, second day running. Stacking a 4th order on top of 3 already-unresolved, stop-less ones isn't disciplined sizing. Resolve the pending three (see banner above), then revisit deployment once you actually know what you're holding.

Your call.

🔄 Rotation Suggestions

Not applicable — zero open positions means nothing to rotate out of.

📚 Today you learned

GTC Orders and the Staleness Trap

A GTC (Good-Til-Canceled) order doesn't expire at the close like a Day order — it sits live until filled or manually canceled, typically for up to 90 days at IBKR. That's convenient for setting an entry and walking away, but it has a blind spot forex doesn't really have the same way: the setup that justified the price can go stale while the order stays live. Your AXTI buy at $58 is the textbook case — placed Aug 4, and the stock has since run to ~$67.90, 17% above your limit. The order itself isn't wrong, but the thesis behind it is now three days and 17% removed from today's chart, and nothing forces you to re-check that before it fills. Treat every GTC order past 48 hours as needing a fresh look, not a "set and forget."

Also today: OCO (One-Cancels-Other) bracket orders — your GOOG buy $365 / sell $408 pair looks like an attempted bracket, but without a stop leg it's just two independent limit orders, not real risk management.

Research output, not financial advice. Past performance does not guarantee future results. No open positions today, so no live price fetch was required for the portfolio itself. Yahoo Finance JSON API (both hosts) and the stooq fallback were all blocked by the network egress proxy this run — pending-order ticker prices (AXTI ~$67.90 Aug 6, GOOG ~$360.13 Aug 5) came from secondary web-search sources, not the primary feed; SPXC's price could not be verified at all. Confirm all three directly in IBKR before acting. Macro and movers figures sourced via web search, cross-checked across multiple outlets where possible. Generated Aug 7, 2026 Kuwait time.
